exam_scheme.note: West Bengal Primary Teacher Eligibility Test (WBTET) is conducted by the West Bengal Board of Primary Education (WBBPE), an autonomous statutory body established under the West Bengal Primary Education Act, 1973, in adherence to National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) guidelines. WBTET establishes statutory eligibility for appointment as Assistant Teachers in Government-Aided, Government-Sponsored, and Junior Basic Primary Schools (Classes I to V) across West Bengal. The examination comprises a single paper of 150 objective Multiple Choice Questions (MCQs) carrying 150 marks for a duration of 150 minutes (2 hours 30 minutes). All questions in non-language sections are bilingual in Bengali and English. There is no negative marking. In adherence to Supreme Court guidelines, professional qualification mandates a 2-year D.El.Ed., 4-year B.El.Ed., or 2-year D.Ed. (Special Education); B.Ed. is not eligible for Primary TET.

competition_benchmarks.note: Official statistics compiled directly from WBBPE statutory declarations, official result summaries, and Board event records. In TET-2023 (held on 24.12.2023, result published on 24.09.2025 vide Memo No. 2121/WBBPE/2025/13T-08/2023), 3,09,054 candidates registered, 2,73,147 candidates appeared across West Bengal examination centres, and 6,754 candidates qualified (pass rate: 2.47%), with 64 candidates securing positions within Ranks 1 to 10. In TET-2022 (held on 11.12.2022, result published on 10.02.2023), 6,19,102 candidates appeared and 1,50,492 qualified (pass rate: 24.31%). Qualifying standard is 60% (90/150 marks) for General/Unreserved category and 55% (82/150 marks) for SC, ST, OBC-A, OBC-B, Differently Abled, Exempted Category, Ex-Servicemen, and Die-in-harness (DH) candidates. Certificate validity is for lifetime.
